subject: KitePay: regional failover — availability window, credit eligibility & postmortem
messages:
From: Sana Iqbal <sana@kitepay.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit.desai@kitepay.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2029 04:25:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected checkout failures 2029-08-16 03:45-04:12 UTC — request for downtime confirmation and credit eligibility

Hi Michael,

We saw a sharp spike in failed checkout transactions and 502/503s for KitePay between 03:45 and 04:12 UTC on 2029-08-16. Failures were observed from EU customers (eu-west-2) and some routed traffic in US-WEST-2 during your automatic regional failover.

Impact summary (customer-visible):
- ~6% of checkout attempts returned immediate 502/503 errors (sampled across three merchants).
- Affected transaction IDs: KP-TR-9a7c, KP-TR-9b1f, KP-TR-9d33 (attached sample).
- We saw elevated P95 latency for successful requests during the window.

We need the following from Redwood:
1) Official confirmation of the availability window (start/end) that you will consider for SLA evaluation.
2) Whether this qualifies for SLA credit under Section 4.2 of our contract — I attached the SLA excerpt (contract-sla-section.pdf).
3) A postmortem or invite for a post-incident call; we want the timeline, cause, and remediation plan.

I've attached an error log snippet (error-sample.log) and marked a couple of impacted merchant IDs. Can you confirm receipt and share an ETA for an initial response?

Thanks,
Sana Iqbal
Head of Platform Reliability, KitePay
Sana Iqbal | sana@kitepay.com | +44 20 7946 0012

Attachment: error-sample.log (text, 12KB)
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Iqbal <sana@kitepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2029 05:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected checkout failures 2029-08-16 03:45-04:12 UTC — request for downtime confirmation and credit eligibility

Hi Sana — thanks for flagging and for the sample logs. Confirmed receipt of the attachment. We're treating this as a priority.

Quick answers / next steps:
- We are pulling the telemetry now and will validate an impact window; preliminary metrics ingestion is under way.
- Karthik and Olga (cc'ed) will own the initial evidence pull (traces, autoscaler events, node evictions) and preserve the relevant logs for your audit.
- We can set up a 30-minute postmortem call today at 15:00 UTC — does that work for you? If not, propose a time and we'll pivot.
- For SLA credit eligibility, we'll map our verified impact window to Section 4.2 and confirm any prorated credit calculations. I'll surface the raw trace bundle and a short timeline in the next 6 hours.

Sana — can you confirm the most critical merchant(s) you want prioritized for trace correlation (merchant IDs or invoice numbers)? That will speed up the RCA.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2029 08:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: KitePay: regional failover — evidence collection plan

Michael / Olga — I'm pulling the following artifacts now and marking them as forensics-preserve (do not auto-delete):
- Per-region instance eviction logs (eu-west-2 / us-west-2), scheduler events, and autoscaler controller trace.
- API gateway request logs (sampled, by merchant ID).
- Request/response traces for the three transaction IDs Sana flagged.
- Pod/container-level resource pressure metrics (CPU, memory, network).

Early hypothesis: a burst of traffic combined with simultaneous scale-in events in eu-west-2 triggered a transient KV cache cold-start pattern and a queueing backlog on a subset of routers which then caused elevated 5xxs until warmup finished. If true, that maps to a partial availability window (not full regional outage). Need trace correlation to be sure.

I attached a short internal impact summary (initial-impact-summary.pdf) with the artifacts list and priority tags. Olga — can you pull the data export to s3://redwood-telemetry/kitepay/2029-08-16/trace-bundle-001 and turn on extended retention for 72 hours?

Sana — if you can confirm the most critical merchant(s) to focus on we'll correlate traces faster. Also, preserve any client-side logs you can share (timing and headers).

Karthik
Director, Incident Response
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: initial-impact-summary.pdf (internal, 230KB)
From: Amit Desai <amit.desai@kitepay.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sana Iqbal <sana@kitepay.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Aug 2029 10:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: KitePay: regional failover — availability window, credit eligibility & postmortem

Thanks — 15:00 UTC works for a call. We'll join with our engineering and payments leads.

A couple of specific asks for the postmortem:
- Please include whether the event will be treated as a single aggregated availability window for SLA calculations or split by region (we're particularly sensitive to eu-west-2).
- If credits apply, we expect the calculation to be consistent with the contract excerpt (Section 4.2). I've attached our annotated SLA PDF for reference.
- Please confirm that Redwood will not purge any of the telemetry we discussed until the postmortem is complete.

We'll expect the initial artifacts at the s3 link Karthik noted and a calendar invite for the 30-minute call.

Regards,
Amit Desai
VP Engineering, KitePay
amit.desai@kitepay.com

-----Forwarded attachment: contract-sla-section.pdf
